overall: The AG found the Peabody School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting its January 24 meeting notice somewhere other than the official City Hall location; other notice concerns were raised but not adjudicated.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the School Committee failed to properly post notice of its January 24 meeting at the official location.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when it failed to properly post notice for its January 24 meeting.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; AG noted concern that open-session notice topics were too general given the many topics actually discussed.
allegations.key_passage: We remind the Committee that the Open Meeting Law requires that every notice must include a listing of topics that the chair reasonably anticipates will be discussed.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; AG noted concern that the executive session notice listing only 'Negotiations update' did not identify a statutory purpose.
allegations.key_passage: We also note our concern with the notice posted for the executive session held on January 24 as the notice simply listed a topic for “Negotiations update.”

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
